title: Me & My Katamari
publisher: Namco / Namco Bandai Games / Electronic Arts
subtitle: A whole world to roll up in the hands
summary: Me & My Katamari is Namco's PSP action-puzzle game, first released in Japan on 22 December 2005. The Prince returns to roll objects into an ever-growing ball, carrying the Katamari idea onto a handheld for the first time. body: Me & My Katamari is Namco's PSP action-puzzle game, first released in Japan on 22 December 2005. The Prince returns to roll objects into an ever-growing ball, carrying the Katamari idea onto a handheld for the first time. Small items make the ball large enough to gather bigger ones, steadily changing the meaning of the surroundings. What first appears to be an obstacle can eventually become another part of the collection. The portable version keeps that transformation of scale while finding a different control arrangement for a machine without two analogue sticks.

The directional pad and face buttons imitate the paired movement of the console games, with shoulder buttons helping execute tight turns. The North American release also offers use of the analogue nub for movement. Learning that arrangement is part of gaining control over a ball whose shape becomes less tidy as objects accumulate. Different times of day and seasons change the central continent across missions. The player returns to familiar surroundings with another target size or condition, discovering how the same place can support a different route through its objects.

Shuhei Kurose and Yutaka Yoshida directed the project, the first Katamari produced without series creator Keita Takahashi. Its music brings together returning series composers, maintaining the playful atmosphere around the Prince's work. Local wireless multiplayer allows friends to visit islands and compete over collections. Western releases followed in 2006. It was also the last Katamari published by Namco before the company merged with Bandai. The handheld adaptation shows how a distinctive physical idea can survive a substantial change in controls when its essential pleasure remains easy to recognise.
story_headings: A whole world to roll up in the hands
Make two sets of buttons move like two hands
Katamari moves beyond its original creator
